recommended_order.reason: Clean imports are the foundation. Fixing sys.path hacks and relative imports changes what mypy can resolve — some suppressed import-not-found errors are caused by path hacks.
recommended_order.resolution: Replace sys.path.insert hacks with proper package installs (pip install -e .) or __init__.py wiring. Convert relative imports to absolute where the package structure supports it. Guard external imports with try/except for optional dependencies.

recommended_order.reason: Once imports are clean, mypy sees the real picture. Adding type annotations makes the I/O review safer because you can verify signatures after async conversion.
recommended_order.resolution: Add return type annotations to untyped functions. Add parameter type annotations where missing. Replace bare generic types (dict, list, tuple) with parameterized versions (dict[str, Any], list[int]). Fix incompatible defaults by using Optional (e.g. content: str | None = None).

recommended_order.reason: Converting sync I/O to async is the most invasive change. It ripples through callers. Clean imports (real call graph) and proper types (verified signatures) make this much safer.
recommended_order.resolution: For each sync function doing I/O: if an async sibling already exists, remove the sync version and update callers. If no async version exists, convert to async (file_open -> aiofiles, subprocess_run -> asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, fs_exists/rglob -> asyncio.to_thread). Update all callers to await the converted function.
